intro.other-analysis: This page keeps the earlier analysis: social support, programme delivery, district needs and priority districts. It uses older methods and data that are not the latest survey.

analysis-filter.title: Choose a place
analysis-filter.text: Choose All Rwanda or one province. The district charts and the Export file follow your choice. Numbers marked National always stay for the whole country.

analysis-findings.title: Read the main numbers
analysis-findings.text: These boxes give the big picture. They show poverty in Rwanda, the district with the most poverty, and how many districts are above the national rate.

analysis-poverty-chart.title: Poverty by District
analysis-poverty-chart.text: Each bar is one district. A longer bar means a higher share of people below the poverty line. The dashed line is the rate for all of Rwanda.

analysis-certainty.title: How Certain Is This?
analysis-certainty.text: Pick a district to see its 95% interval, sample size, reliability and whether it is really different from Rwanda. A wide interval means the survey is less sure about that district.

analysis-chart-eye.title: The eye icon
analysis-chart-eye.text: Look for the eye next to a chart name. Click it to read, in simple words, what the chart shows and what to be careful about.

analysis-chart-ai.title: The sparkles icon
analysis-chart-ai.text: Click the purple sparkles to ask the AI a question about the chart. Always check the answer against the source.

analysis-changes.title: Poverty Changes
analysis-changes.text: The empty dot is the rate in 2016/17. The full dot is the rate in 2023/24. The space between them shows how much poverty went up or down.

analysis-finance.title: Financial Inclusion
analysis-finance.text: Imagine 100 adults in Rwanda. Each slice shows how many use banks or other money services. These numbers are for the whole country.

financial-intro.title: Two official sources
financial-intro.text: This page keeps BNR provider data and NISR FinScope household-survey evidence separate because they measure different things.

financial-guide.title: Read the figures safely
financial-guide.text: Use the source labels before comparing figures. The BNR dashboard is live provider information; FinScope is a survey of adults.

financial-bnr.title: BNR live dashboard
financial-bnr.text: Use this embedded official dashboard for the current provider-reported view. If it cannot load here, open it in a new tab.

financial-finscope.title: NISR FinScope evidence
financial-finscope.text: These charts show published FinScope survey estimates and trends. They are not a copy of the BNR dashboard.

upload-intro.title: Safe uploads
upload-intro.text: This page accepts published aggregate indicators only. Personal, household, and customer data do not belong here.

upload-form.title: Submit a draft
upload-form.text: Add the official source details and use the CSV template. The file is checked before it is sent for review.

upload-preview.title: Check the rows
upload-preview.text: Review the first parsed rows before submitting. Fix any source, period, or value error in the file first.

upload-review.title: Approval controls
upload-review.text: Drafts do not change public charts. A platform administrator can approve or reject them with a recorded note.

analysis-data-note.title: The amber warning icon
analysis-data-note.text: An amber triangle under a chart opens a data note. It tells you, in plain words, where our figure differs from the one NISR published, or why a year is missing, so you know how far to trust it. Click it to read the note.

analysis-support.title: Poverty & Social Support
analysis-support.text: This part compares poverty with VUP. VUP is a government programme that helps poor families. Poverty counts people. VUP counts poor households. So do not subtract one from the other.

support-views.title: Three ways to look
support-views.text: Compare shows every district in rows. Prioritize shows districts on one chart, so you can find which ones to study first. Districts shows a table you can search and sort.

support-scatter.title: Read the Prioritize chart
support-scatter.text: Each dot is a district. Dots higher up have more poverty. Dots further right have more VUP. The top-left area, Review first, has high poverty and low VUP. Click a dot to see more and to start an investigation.

analysis-needs.title: Compare a district with Rwanda

analysis-priority.title: Priority Districts
analysis-priority.text: These districts have the highest poverty. They are a good place to start looking. They are not a final decision about who gets help.

problem.title: The problem, and where the data comes from
problem.text: Ireme Insight answers one question for NISR: which districts have the highest poverty, and what happens next. The headline figures are official NISR releases - the EICV7 2023/24 household survey for poverty, and published FinScope and provider aggregates for finance. Nothing on this page is estimated by a model.

evidence.title: How sure the evidence is
evidence.text: Each district figure carries a design-based 95% interval, the number of households behind it and a reliability grade. Where a district falls inside the national interval the page says it is not clearly different from Rwanda, rather than ranking it. Sources, periods, populations and methods are listed on Data & Methodology, and differences from published figures stay visible as data notes.

compare.title: Comparing options, honestly
compare.text: A same-budget comparison of support approaches is not validated yet, so this screen sets out what such a comparison needs and shows no invented numbers. When scenarios exist they will be labelled as scenarios, never as outcomes.

action.title: From evidence to action
action.text: This is the request queue: an analyst asks for a check, a programme account accepts or declines with a reason, an agent reports from the field, and the answer returns. Every record here is a demonstration record, so its counts are never programme performance figures.

actionAnalyst.text: Programme teams work the queue in their own panel, which your role does not open. Here you see each request's status next to the poverty figure that prompted it, which is the honest view for a national analyst.

report.title: What a report can prove
report.text: Reports, review and export run through the governed research API. If it is not connected, this workspace says so plainly rather than showing a result or a green label. Published reports keep their impact limits next to the export control.

evidence-check.title: Check the evidence
evidence-check.subtitle: See where a number comes from, how reliable it is, and what still needs review.
evidence-check.purpose: Follow any headline figure back to its official source and see how much sampling uncertainty it carries.
evidence-check.source: NISR EICV7 2023/24 published aggregates, loaded into this repository from the official register on the Data & Methodology page.
evidence-check.period: 2023/24 survey year. The earlier rates are NISR's modelled 2016/17 estimates.
evidence-check.population: Poverty measures describe people. VUP participation describes surveyed poor households. The two are never subtracted from each other.
evidence-check.geography: Rwanda as a whole and each district.
evidence-check.denominator: Weighted population for poverty shares; weighted surveyed poor households for reported VUP participation.
evidence-check.method: Design-based estimation under the stratified multi-stage cluster design, with Taylor-series linearisation for variance and 95% intervals on design degrees of freedom.
evidence-check.systemState: Intervals are calculated in this repository and shown wherever a district figure appears. Independent scientific review is still outstanding, so results stay labelled as pending review rather than certified.
evidence-check.limitation: Districts with few surveyed households give wide intervals, and a difference inside the interval is not evidence of a real difference. Licensed microdata is never sent to the browser.

support-compare.title: Compare support options
support-compare.subtitle: Explore which approach might reach more households at the same assumed budget.
support-compare.purpose: Compare two support approaches under one assumed budget before anyone commits resources to either.
support-compare.source: Not available. No approved budget, unit cost or versioned targeting rule is loaded in this build.
support-compare.method: A comparison would need a coverage baseline, an agreed budget line and a reviewed rule set, then a stated simulation model with its assumptions beside every result.
support-compare.systemState: Not implemented. The application shows no comparison figures, so nothing here can be read as a simulated outcome.
support-compare.limitation: Until the inputs above are approved and reviewed, any number produced would be a guess. This screen states the requirement instead.

resilience.title: Understand financial resilience
resilience.subtitle: Read what people report using, keep the two financial sources apart, and see what is still missing.
resilience.purpose: Show financial access from two different official sources and keep their measures separate instead of blending them into one rate.
resilience.source: NISR FinScope 2024 household survey, and the BNR/NBR provider dashboard snapshot. Both are published aggregates.
resilience.period: FinScope 2024. The provider snapshot carries its own retrieval date on the page.
resilience.population: Adults in Rwanda: those interviewed in the survey, and those appearing in regulated provider records. The groups overlap but are not the same.
resilience.geography: National, with district comparisons from the survey side.
resilience.denominator: Surveyed adults for FinScope shares; provider customer records for BNR counts.
resilience.method: Published aggregates are shown as released. This application does not re-derive them or combine them with survey poverty.
resilience.systemState: Access measures are available. Resilience measures - savings, insurance against a shock, whether a household can cover an unexpected expense - are not in the loaded dataset, so the application does not report them.
resilience.limitation: Having an account does not show financial resilience. Access and provider counts cannot be added, compared as one figure, or read as a poverty result.

action-tracking.title: Follow action and results
action-tracking.subtitle: See how an evidence-based request moves to programme follow-up.
action-tracking.purpose: Trace one request from a survey finding, through a programme decision and field work, to the answer that comes back to the analyst.
action-tracking.source: Workflow records created in this demonstration build. The survey evidence that prompts a request comes from NISR EICV7.
action-tracking.population: Programme requests, their assignees and recorded outcomes.
action-tracking.method: Each request keeps a status history with the actor and note at every step, and a completed request returns an outcome to the analyst.
action-tracking.systemState: The queue runs in the browser and is stored on this device. It is not connected to a government system, so waiting, in-progress and completed counts are demonstration figures, never programme performance.
action-tracking.limitation: Requests, agents and outcomes shown here are sample records unless a server-backed workflow with row-level security is authorised and connected. Draft and demonstration records are not counted as verified results.

vup-rules.title: Understand VUP screening
vup-rules.subtitle: Check an application against reviewed rules, with a person making the decision.
vup-rules.purpose: Show how a VUP application would be screened against published rules, leaving the decision with a named officer.
vup-rules.source: Not available. The approved rule text, its legal source and its version are not loaded in this build.
vup-rules.systemState: The roster shows members on record. It applies no screening rule and issues no eligibility verdict, because nothing here has been verified against an approved source.
vup-rules.limitation: Rules must be transcribed from an approved instrument, versioned and reviewed by the programme before any pre-screening is shown. A member list is a register, not a decision.

referral-followup.title: Connect people with opportunities
referral-followup.subtitle: Match skills and support needs to suitable services, then track the follow-up.
referral-followup.purpose: Track an opportunity from a matching step to an application, an interview and an outcome that a person confirms.
referral-followup.source: Opportunity and application records created in this demonstration build.
referral-followup.systemState: Applications move through staged states with a note at each step. No vacancy is live and no placement is confirmed by an outside employer.
referral-followup.limitation: Catalogued opportunities are demonstration entries, not vacancies, and a tracked outcome here is not evidence that a person's income changed.

quality-checks.title: How we check the numbers
quality-checks.subtitle: Read statistical checks, source comparison and unresolved differences.
quality-checks.purpose: Show which checks run automatically, what they catch, and what still needs a human reviewer.
quality-checks.source: The official source register on this page records each file's publisher, period, geography, licence and load status. Report wording is checked against the figures it describes.
quality-checks.method: Estimates are computed from published aggregates with the survey design respected. Wording checks flag a sentence that contradicts its own figure, and the check is recorded rather than hidden.
quality-checks.systemState: Machine checks run in this repository and their results are readable. A release stays blocked until the governed API and a named reviewer approve it, and that review is not complete.
quality-checks.limitation: Automated checks find wording that contradicts the data. They are not an independent scientific certification, and where our figure differs from a published one the page shows a data note instead of replacing either number.

model-evaluation.title: Understand the model
model-evaluation.subtitle: See out-of-sample results, calibration, fairness and limitations.
model-evaluation.purpose: Show how a targeting model performed on data it never saw, and where it fails.
model-evaluation.source: Not available. No trained model, holdout set or evaluation report is shipped in this build.
model-evaluation.systemState: No accuracy, calibration or fairness figure appears anywhere in the application, and no household is classified by a model.
model-evaluation.limitation: A model card needs a holdout grouped by survey cluster, leakage tests, calibration and a fairness review before any performance number can be published.
